observedBehaviour: A shape container does not centre a child wider than itself: it clamps the child's left edge to its own, so the child's centre lands half the overflow to the RIGHT of where centring would put it. Measured at 2.2.1 with a 60 pt container holding a 140 pt spacer positioned at LayerAlign.CENTER with dx = 0 — container x 0.0 and child x 0.0, container centre 30.0 and child centre 70.0, a drift of 40.0 pt against an overflow of 80.0 pt. This is the horizontal twin of the known vertical top-clamp: the same rule on the other axis, and the reason a masthead built by centring an over-wide mark inside a narrow band drifts right rather than sitting on the band's axis.

minimalReproduction.arrangement: A 60 pt wide shape container with ClipPolicy.OVERFLOW_VISIBLE holding a 140 pt wide spacer at LayerAlign.CENTER, dx = 0. The same probe's vertical half answers the over-tall case, so one run settles both axes. A spacer is used rather than an empty shape container because ShapeContainerNode is rejected at build time unless it has at least one layer.

workaround: Offset by minus half the overflow to put the two centres on one axis — for a child of width w in a container of width c, dx = -(w - c) / 2. Better still, size the container to the child rather than correcting after the fact: the clamp only bites when the child is larger than what holds it.

sourceRun.note: The brand mark drifted right inside its band. The run measured it from rendered pixels, recorded it in the revision's architecture plan, and had no probe to promote it with; this record is that probe's answer.
